gap: No result ChatGPT got states today's maker-store prices of the 2026 models beside the models they replace: the EcoFlow DELTA 3000 Gen4 is now $1,299 ($423/kWh), cheaper than the older DELTA 3 Ultra at $1,369 ($446/kWh) while taking 1,000 W of solar against 800 W and weighing 26 kg against 32.7 kg, though it ships only in early January 2027; and BLUETTI's new Apex 200 costs the same per kWh as the Elite 200 V2 it sits above ($429 vs $432/kWh).
standout_why: Compared with homepowerfacts.com/new-power-stations (launch and list prices for the new models, a list price for one older 'closest' model each, no per-kWh math, no current prices), stationarena.com/new-releases (launch prices only, states outright that it does not compare new models to predecessors on price), and energysage.com solar-generators-overview (older models only, list prices, no 2026 dating). None gives a same-day maker-store price for a new model and its predecessor, none prices per kWh, and the DELTA 3000 Gen4 figure they and ChatGPT carry ($1,699 preorder, 'late November' shipping) is out of date.
decides: It reverses one row of ChatGPT's table and sharpens two others. DELTA 3000 Gen4 vs DELTA 3 Ultra: the new one now wins on price, solar input and weight, so 'older model can be a better deal' is wrong today; the only reason to buy the Ultra is that it ships in early December versus January 2027 for the Gen4. Apex 200 vs Elite 200 V2: per-kWh parity ($429 vs $432), so the Apex 200 is worth buying when you want its 3,200 W output, 3,000 W solar input and expansion, not to save money. Anker S5000 vs F3800 Plus: the S5000 is $517/kWh vs $625/kWh and the F3800 Plus is sold out on Anker's store, so the new one wins unless you need 6,000 W. EcoFlow TITAN 5000: ChatGPT's 'from around $2,499' is the Classic version with 4,000 W; the 7,200 W standard TITAN 5000 is $3,199.
